prs.title: fix(streamable-http): wait for post_writer before yielding
prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Race condition in streamable_http's post_writer: the task group starts post_writer with tg.start_soon() and the caller proceeds to yield the transport immediately, without waiting for post_writer to actually enter its stream context and be ready to receive. Messages written to write_stream right after startup can be sent before post_writer is listening, causing lost writes / hangs. Both PRs fix this identically: give post_writer a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context managers, so the caller (via tg.start(...)) blocks until post_writer is actually ready before yielding. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string parameter whose annotation isn't literally `str`, including `str | None`/Optional[str] unions — so a valid string argument that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "true", '["a"]') gets silently decoded into None/int/bool/list instead of being passed through as a string. Both PRs add a predicate to skip json.loads for such union annotations. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks each union member for frozenset membership in {str,int,float,bool,NoneType} without unwrapping Annotated, so the idiomatic FastMCP pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` still misidentifies the Annotated-wrapped member as a non-simple type and continues to call json.loads, leaving the corruption bug unfixed for that common shape. #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated() step before classifying union members, so it correctly detects Optional[str] even when wrapped in Annotated/Field, covering a real-world case #2032's diff does not.

members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: Both PRs fix the same root-cause bug: pickling an MCPError/UrlElicitationRequiredError loses or breaks data because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), where self.args=(code, message, data) doesn't match subclass constructors (issue #2431). #2478 fixes this generically by adding a module-level _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) dispatcher that special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (via from_error) and falls back to from_error_data for all other MCPError subclasses — implying a __reduce__ on the MCPError base class routes through this dispatcher. #2555 fixes it by adding a __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError that reconstructs from (self._elicitations, self.message), bypassing the base-class mechanism entirely via Python's method resolution (a subclass-defined __reduce__ always wins over the parent's). members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs rewrite the exact same block in `RequestResponder.cancel()` in src/mcp/shared/session.py (both diffs are based on the identical blob 243eef5ae6, and both replace the code immediately following `self._completed = True  # Mark as completed so it's removed from in_flight` / the `# Send an error response to indicate cancellation` block). They are two competing fixes for the same defect: the old code sent a stray error response when a request got cancelled. #2493 removes that response-sending code outright (and adjusts server.py's duplicate-suppression comment to reflect that per spec no response should ever be sent for a cancelled request). #2514 instead replaces the same block with logic to send a `notifications/cancelled` message on timeout/caller-initiated cancellation. members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in streamable_http's post_writer: the task group starts post_writer with tg.start_soon() and the caller proceeds to yield the transport immediately, without waiting for post_writer to actually enter its stream context and be ready to receive. Messages written to write_stream right after startup can be sent before post_writer is listening, causing lost writes / hangs. Both PRs fix this identically: give post_writer a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context managers, so the caller (via tg.start(...)) blocks until post_writer is actually ready before yielding.

members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both modify the same write_stream memory-object-stream initialization in stdio.py, targeting the underlying issue that a zero-capacity (rendezvous) stream forces every write to block until read, which can stall a handler trying to queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 addresses this generically by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as new constructor parameters, both still defaulting to 0 so behavior is unchanged unless a caller opts in. #2654 addresses it directly by hardcoding the write_stream capacity to 1, fixing the default behavior for every caller without any config change.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: Both PRs fix the same root-cause bug: pickling an MCPError/UrlElicitationRequiredError loses or breaks data because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), where self.args=(code, message, data) doesn't match subclass constructors (issue #2431). #2478 fixes this generically by adding a module-level _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) dispatcher that special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (via from_error) and falls back to from_error_data for all other MCPError subclasses — implying a __reduce__ on the MCPError base class routes through this dispatcher. #2555 fixes it by adding a __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError that reconstructs from (self._elicitations, self.message), bypassing the base-class mechanism entirely via Python's method resolution (a subclass-defined __reduce__ always wins over the parent's). Since a subclass __reduce__ takes precedence over the base class's, merging both would make #2478's special-case branch for UrlElicitationRequiredError inside _restore_mcp_error dead code — the two changes directly conflict in the same file/class hierarchy and address the identical failure mode.
